references.text: Jesus was in Simon's boat and taught from there, which sets the context for the miraculous catch and the need to call the other boat.
The preceding verse describes the enormous catch that threatened to tear the net apart, leading them to signal their partners in the other boat to come and help.

As a result of the great catch—both boats were filled to the brim—Simon Peter and his companions, including James and John (the sons of Zebedee), were overwhelmed with awe and called to become fishers of people.
A parallel event after the resurrection where Jesus again commands the disciples to cast the net on the other side, resulting in an overwhelming catch, reminiscent of the great catch in Luke 5.
The great catch of 153 fish in John 21 mirrors the miraculous abundance of fish that filled both boats in Luke 5:7.
James and John, the sons of Zebedee, are referred to as Simon's 'metochoi' (partners/companions)—the same ones called from the other boat in verse 7.
Matthew's account of the calling of the first disciples, including two boats with fishermen (Simon, Andrew, James, and John), who left everything to follow Jesus.
Mark's parallel account of the calling of the first disciples by the Sea of Galilee, where two pairs of brothers in separate boats are called to follow Jesus.
